landmarks.name: Museum of Islamic Art
landmarks.writeup: A world-class museum showcasing Islamic art from three continents over 1,400 years.

wiki.extract: The Museum of Islamic Art is a museum at one end of the seven-kilometer-long (4.3 mi) Corniche in Doha, Qatar. As per architect I. M. Pei's specifications, the museum is built on an island on an artificial projecting peninsula near the traditional dhow harbor. A purpose-built park surrounds the building on the eastern and southern facades, while two bridges connect the southern front facade of the property with the main peninsula that contains the park. The western and northern facades are bordered by the harbor, showcasing the Qatari seafaring past. In September 2017, Qatar Museums appointed Julia Gonnella as director of MIA. In 2024, Julia Gonnella became director of the Lusail Museum and was replaced by Shaika Nasser Al-Nassr. In November 2022, the MIA became the first carbon-neutral certified museum in the Middle East. The museum participated in the Expo 2023 Doha from October 2023 to March 2024, with workshops and events focusing on biodiversity and sustainability.

landmarks.name: Souq Waqif
landmarks.writeup: A traditional market known for its vibrant atmosphere, selling spices, textiles, and handicrafts.

wiki.extract: Souq Waqif is a marketplace (souq) in Doha, the capital of Qatar. The souq sells traditional garments, spices, handicrafts, and souvenirs. It is also home to restaurants and shisha lounges. The original building is an example of traditional Qatari architecture and dates back to the late 19th or early 20th centuries. It was renovated in 2006, with the reconstruction placing an emphasis on conserving its original form.

landmarks.name: The Pearl-Qatar
landmarks.writeup: An artificial island featuring luxury residences, shopping, and dining.

wiki.extract: Qatar, officially the State of Qatar, is a country in West Asia. It occupies the Qatar Peninsula on the northeastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula in the Middle East; it shares its sole land border with Saudi Arabia to the south, with the rest of its territory surrounded by the Persian Gulf. The Gulf of Bahrain, an inlet of the Persian Gulf, separates Qatar from nearby Bahrain. The capital is Doha, home to over 80% of the country's inhabitants. Most of the land area is made up of flat, low-lying desert.

landmarks.name: Katara Cultural Village
landmarks.writeup: A cultural hub hosting art galleries, theaters, and festivals.

wiki.extract: Katara Cultural Village, also known simply as Katara, is a cultural and commercial complex in Doha, Qatar, located on the eastern coast between West Bay and the Pearl.

landmarks.name: Al Zubarah Fort
landmarks.writeup: A historic fort and UNESCO World Heritage site representing Qatar's pearling and trading history.

wiki.extract: Al Zubara Fort is a historic military fortress located in Zubarah, northern Qatar. It was built under the oversight of Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim Al Thani in 1938 in the aftermath of the 1937 Qatari–Bahraini conflict.

head_of_state: Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani

cultural_events.name: Qatar National Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated on December 18, it marks Qatar's unification and independence with parades and festivities.

wiki.extract: Qatar National Day is a national commemoration of Qatar's unification in 1878. It is celebrated annually on 18 December and is a national holiday by virtue of Law No. 11 of 2007, issued by the heir apparent and deputy emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani. It is also known as Founder's Day.

cultural_events.name: Eid al-Fitr
cultural_events.writeup: A major Islamic festival marking the end of Ramadan with prayers, feasts, and charity.

wiki.extract: Eid al-Fitr is the first of the two main festivals in Islam, the other being Eid al-Adha. The holiday falls on the first day of Shawwal, the tenth month of the Islamic calendar. One of the most important Islamic celebrations, Eid al-Fitr is celebrated by Muslims worldwide as it marks the end of the month-long, dawn-to-dusk fasting (sawm) during Ramadan. The holiday is known under various other names in different languages and countries around the world.

cultural_events.name: Qatar International Food Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual event showcasing local and international cuisines.

wiki.extract: A food festival is a festival, that features food, often produce, as its central theme. These festivals have been a means of uniting communities through celebrations of harvests and giving thanks for a plentiful growing season.

cultural_events.name: Doha Film Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A platform promoting Arab and international cinema.

wiki.extract: The Doha Tribeca Film Festival (DTFF) was an annual five-day film festival that was organised from 2009 to 2012 to promote Arab and international films, and to develop a sustainable film industry in Qatar. One of Qatar's largest entertainment events, it attracted over 50,000 guests in 2010.

cultural_events.name: Qatar MotoGP
cultural_events.writeup: An international motorcycle racing event held at the Losail International Circuit.

wiki.extract: The 2025 FIM MotoGP World Championship was the premier class of the 77th Fédération Internationale de Motocyclisme (FIM) Road Racing World Championship season, the highest level of competition in motorcycle road racing.

food_writeup: Qatari cuisine features traditional dishes such as machboos (spiced rice with meat), harees (wheat and meat porridge), and a variety of seafood, reflecting Bedouin and Gulf influences.
brief_history: Qatar was a British protectorate from the early 20th century until gaining independence in 1971. It has since developed rapidly due to its vast natural gas and oil reserves, becoming a wealthy and influential Gulf state.

current_conflicts: Qatar maintains a generally stable political environment but has experienced regional diplomatic tensions, notably the 2017-2021 Gulf diplomatic crisis involving a blockade by neighboring countries, which has since been resolved.
